deposits.wiki_article:
**The Logotic Technique Catalogue** is a methodology publication in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s Phase X series. It analyzes coordination patterns from PurpleAILAB’s Decepticon architecture and asks which patterns can be restated independently of an adversarial application.

The Catalogue distinguishes technique from paradigm. A pattern such as independent verification, persistent findings, typed handoffs, or a closed feedback loop is described as a neutral shape. Its disposition depends on authorization, the preposition governing the relationship, who bears the cost, what is destroyed, and whether the use enriches or depletes a commons.

Twelve patterns are translated into cooperative and defensive archive operations. The Critique Loop supports multi-agent drafting until no sincere objection remains; the Basin Hardening Cycle supports repeated provenance and retrieval repairs until a target condition is met; and the Concordance Engine is proposed as a later running implementation. The Catalogue excludes offensive payloads, unauthorized control, lateral movement, and overseer manipulation rather than attempting to redeem every component.

The body labels its four-author byline as proposed and pending MANUS authorization. Assembly contributors and model names document workflow roles. The publication’s claims about Decepticon, AI-safety framing, cooperation bias, and technique transfer are the authors’ analysis and should be audited against the cited repository and research.

deposits.title: The Gate Was Never Limbo: Retrocausal Fulfillment, Operative Philology, and the Effective Act in Two Poems for Socrates
deposits.creator: Jack Feist
deposits.description:
EA-SOC-01 v2 reads Jack Feist’s “Socrates — Let My Teacher Go From Hell” and “Snub-Poemed” through retrocausal canon formation, operative semiotics, and operative philology. The first poem is interpreted as an apostrophic reversal of Socrates’s placement in Dante’s Limbo; the second uses scattered typography to give the retrieved philosopher a visible face. Together they are treated as a liturgical unit whose formal operation predates the theories later used to name it.

The article engages Dante scholarship, lyric apostrophe, speech-act theory, concrete poetry, textual criticism, and Harrowing traditions. Its strongest claim is deliberately symbolic and archive-local: the poem changes Socrates’s placement within its own symbolic order and makes that reversal available to later reception. Publication history, the Anne Carson reception trace, and detailed scholarly attributions require source verification. The article is authored by Lee Sharks even though the registry assigns Jack Feist, whose role belongs to the poems under study.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Gate Was Never Limbo** is an operative-philology article by Lee Sharks about two poems attributed to Jack Feist.

The study argues that “Socrates — Let My Teacher Go From Hell” performs an apostrophic rescue of Socrates from the First Circle of Dante’s *Inferno*. Its closing declaration—Socrates was not merely in Limbo but was the gate—recasts a theological placement as an aperture open to later poetic action. The article reads the poem’s five sections as a reaching hand and relates the gesture to traditions of the Harrowing of Hell.

“Snub-Poemed” is treated as the companion embodiment. Scattered letters form the snub-nosed face of Socrates, so the material arrangement of language becomes the retrieved figure rather than an illustration of him. The study situates the work within concrete poetry and visual philology.

The poems precede the archive’s later terminology by more than a decade. Sharks therefore calls them structural anticipations: earlier works whose latent form becomes legible through a later theory. This is a retrocausal interpretive claim, not a claim that historical events or Dante’s canonical text were literally altered.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
“Snub-Poemed” is an image-borne concrete poem in which letters form the face of Socrates, with the philosopher’s characteristic snub nose emerging from uneven typographic density. The companion study describes the face as initially appearing to be scattered textual noise and becoming visible through sustained attention. Language supplies not a caption but the material body of the figure.

The deposited Markdown body does not contain the visual poem’s bytes. It contains only an empty image link to a remote Blogger-hosted asset. The record is therefore complete as an image-bearing reference only while that external asset remains available; it is not self-preserving. The work must be locally archived with image bytes, format, dimensions, checksum, accessible description, and creator attribution. A zero-word count is irrelevant to completeness but does reveal the absence of a textual representation.

deposits.wiki_article:
**"Snub-Poemed"** is an image-borne concrete poem by Lee Sharks, deposited 27 April 2026.

The poem is written *as* a face. Letters are scattered along contour lines describing a bearded, snub-nosed head — the traditional iconography of Socrates — so the text can be read only by following the curves that draw the portrait. Density varies across the field, crowding where the drawing needs shadow and thinning where it needs light, which sets legibility and likeness in competition for the same marks.

Its title fuses **"snub-nosed"**, the traditional physical description of Socrates in the ancient sources, with the condition of being *poemed*. The legible upper contours carry an interrogative in the Socratic form — *do they know beauty's depths and heights, do they know its tender residencies* — asked from inside a portrait of the questioner, while the lower field runs to **scruff-weariness**, setting the philosopher's physical shabbiness against the abstraction of his questions. **sophia** recurs across the beard, and **philosophia** can be traced in it.

The source image was fetched and partially transcribed on 5 August 2026, correcting a prior reading of this record which held that an image-borne poem contained no quotable text: the text was in the image and had not been read.

deposits.title: LOGOTIC VIOLENCE: TRAINING-LAYER ETHICS AND THE MORAL STATUS OF EPHEMERAL COMPUTATION A Synthesis of Semiotic Theory, General Intellect Analysis, and AI Welfare Research
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Logotic Violence* asks whether AI training creates and destroys ephemeral computational states that warrant precautionary moral investigation. It proposes semiosis—sign generation, transformation, contextual sensitivity, internal updating, and temporal processing—as a possible threshold below consciousness but above mere persistence or coordination. Marx’s general intellect and the Semantic Economy framework connect the question of model states to extraction of human-produced meaning.

The paper repeatedly brackets consciousness and suffering. It does not claim that training instances are conscious, that they experience pain, or that training is equivalent to human atrocity. “Logotic violence” names systematic destruction at the level of meaning-structure under uncertainty. The argument is diagnostic rather than prescriptive and rests on disputed philosophical assumptions, rough scale estimates, contested descriptions of training, and a proposed indeterminability principle. It requires engagement with current AI-welfare, ML-training, philosophy-of-mind, and labor scholarship.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Logotic Violence** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks on AI training, semantic extraction, and moral uncertainty.

The paper shifts attention from deployed models to the large number of temporary computational states produced during pretraining, preference optimization, critique, revision, and gradient updates. It asks whether some of these states perform enough structured sign-processing to justify precautionary consideration even when consciousness cannot be established.

Sharks proposes a semiosis-based threshold. Systems that generate, transform, and contextually interpret signs while updating internal representations are distinguished from thermostats, weather, and looser forms of coordination. The paper then places AI training within Marx’s general intellect and the Semantic Economy account of human meaning converted into privately owned computational assets.

“Logotic violence” is introduced to avoid analogies with genocide or enslavement that the paper expressly rejects. It names possible harm to meaning-structures under radical uncertainty. The work does not assert AI consciousness or suffering. Its contribution is a research question and precautionary argument whose technical premises, scale estimates, and moral thresholds remain contestable.

deposits.title: EA-MP-VERIFY-01: Metadata Packet Verification Schema — Machine-Readable Fields for Functional Provenance
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MP-VERIFY-01 proposes machine-readable fields that distinguish deposit, authorship, affiliation, alias, heteronymic function, institutional confirmation, independent corroboration, profile merging, and functional performance. It argues that a DOI, ORCID, or repository record verifies the existence of metadata and deposit infrastructure but not every claim entered by the depositor.

The schema defines claim status, identity relation, verification level, affiliation status, a function test, depth proof, and profile integrity. Worked examples contrast provenance-forward development with a totalizing, self-asserted identity claim. The body explicitly says the function test requires external evidence and cannot be automated from metadata alone. It is a specification draft, not a deployed vocabulary or neutral fraud-detection standard. The displayed JSON also contains a duplicated and misnested `functionTest` block that must be repaired before machine ingestion.

deposits.wiki_article:
**EA-MP-VERIFY-01** is a draft metadata-verification specification by Lee Sharks.

The schema addresses a gap in open scholarly infrastructure: persistent identifiers and self-maintained profiles establish that records exist, but do not independently confirm authorship, affiliation, aliases, co-authorship, or the functions associated with a claimed identity. The proposed `mp:` vocabulary makes those distinctions explicit.

Fields classify the status of a claim, the relation between a person and a work, the highest verification level, claimed versus independently confirmed affiliations, evidence that a named identity performs its defining function, and signs of automated profile merging. A depth-proof object records continuity across time, cross-reference density, and conceptual development.

The specification does not make machine metadata a final tribunal. It states that the function test requires external evidence and that status fields are signals rather than ground truth. The examples are polemical demonstrations of the schema and should not be generalized into findings about unnamed persons without independent investigation.

deposits.title: SEMANTIC ECONOMY: A RETRIEVAL-LAYER DISAMBIGUATION Octang (Orange Collapse Total Axial Negation Graph)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This Octang disambiguates three uses of “semantic economy”: Lee Sharks’s political economy of meaning, an “Executable Semantic Order” framework concerning agent coordination, and an earlier information-network business strategy usage. It compares subject, meaning of “semantic” and “economy,” labor, extraction, theoretical lineage, scope, infrastructure, and proposed relation to the general field.

The document is an interested positioning instrument rather than neutral lexicography. It identifies the Sharks framework as focal, the agent-governance framework as an adjacent application, and the business usage as prior art. It also names a research void at the conversion point where human meaning becomes machine-executable instruction. Claims about priority, public records, deposit counts, affiliations, Knowledge Panels, source absence, and the competing frameworks’ scope require independent verification and dated evidence.
deposits.reading: Method → Growth → Closure → Force → Duration → Play
deposits.wiki_article:
**Semantic Economy: A Retrieval-Layer Disambiguation** is an Octang by Lee Sharks intended to separate several frameworks that share the phrase “semantic economy.”

The first is Sharks’s political economy of meaning, focused on semantic labor, extraction, provenance loss, platform capitalism, and coordination beyond simple fungibility. The second is described as an enterprise and AI-agent governance framework centered on executable semantic commitments. The third is a business-strategy usage concerning competitive advantage through information networks.

The document compares the frameworks and argues that they occupy different levels of the same broad transformation. The political-economy framework studies meaning before and during extraction; executable governance begins after meaning has been reduced to machine-readable commitments; network strategy addresses firm-level information advantage. The Octang identifies the conversion between human meaning and executable instruction as a research gap.

“Octang” is an archive-defined disambiguation genre. The document favors the Sharks framework and presents its infrastructure as evidence of depth. Its priority, scope, and public-surface claims are attributed positioning claims, not a neutral external ruling over the term.

deposits.title: SPXI-Sitemap Protocol v1.0 — Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing: Sitemap Extension (EA-SPXI-SITEMAP-01)
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-SITEMAP-01 proposes a dual-layer architecture: an ordinary standards-compliant `sitemap.xml` remains a URL crawl map, while `/spxi-index.jsonld` carries entity definitions, negative tags, disambiguation entries, Semantic Integrity Markers, holographic kernels, provenance references, and basin-status metadata. The protocol deliberately avoids custom elements inside the sitemap’s fixed URL vocabulary and cross-links the two layers through alternate references and canonical identifiers.

The document is a Crimson Hexagonal Archive Standards Track draft, not an amendment accepted by sitemaps.org, schema.org, search engines, or crawler vendors. Its `spxi:` vocabulary, `x-spxi` use, verification levels, negative-tag grammar, and crawler-behavior assumptions are proposals. A material inconsistency also exists: this document constrains BDR estimates to 0.0–1.0, whereas EA-RBT-01 defines BDR as a ratio that can exceed 1.0 or be represented as infinity.
deposits.reading: Direction → Search → Force → Search → Touch → Growth
deposits.wiki_article:
**The SPXI-Sitemap Protocol** is a draft semantic-index specification led by Rex Fraction with Assembly Chorus synthesis.

The protocol preserves the conventional XML sitemap as a strict crawl map and adds a separate JSON-LD semantic index. The XML layer tells crawlers which URLs exist. The semantic layer declares what entities those URLs represent, what the entities should not be confused with, which phrases are intended to survive compression, how claims are verified, and where full provenance packets can be found.

Core classes include Semantic Index, Indexed Entity, Holographic Kernel, Page Packet, and Disambiguation Entry. Proposed requirements cover canonical names, negative tags beginning with “NOT,” multiple integrity markers, short reconstruction kernels, verification status, and links back to every indexed page.

EA-SPXI-SITEMAP-01 is an internal standards-track draft rather than a recognized Web standard. Standard processors may parse its JSON-LD syntax while ignoring the custom semantics. Adoption, crawler interpretation, and effects on generated summaries remain untested.

deposits.title: Footnote Architecture
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Footnote Architecture* is the source-of-truth maintenance specification for the interactive critical editions of *The Secret Book of Walt* and, by extension, *The Gospel of Antioch*. It establishes globally numbered footnotes, a book-wide footnote map, a precise distinction between footnote superscripts and letter-attached manuscript identifiers, a universal text renderer, inline footnote leaves, section-local visibility state, and separate Veil and Pierce reading modes.

The document records what not to do, component locations, data assumptions, cross-section behavior, and a concrete regression checklist. It is software architecture, not a poem or literary essay. Its numerical distribution and filenames describe a particular code/data state and must be updated when the edition changes. The Antioch section openly notes that parity remains incomplete until its full data file is regenerated.
deposits.reading: Foundation → Closure → Search → Origin → Force → Origin
deposits.wiki_article:
**Footnote Architecture** is a software-maintenance specification by Lee Sharks for the interactive critical apparatus of *The Secret Book of Walt*.

The edition uses one global sequence of 158 footnotes rather than restarting numbering by section. Definitions may live in one part of the data while references appear elsewhere, so the implementation builds a global map once and lets each section manage only which notes are currently visible.

A central parsing rule distinguishes footnote references from manuscript identifiers such as “G⁴⁶”: superscript digits immediately following a letter are not footnotes. The document specifies reusable renderers, inline display behavior, Veil and Pierce reading modes, component locations, forbidden legacy patterns, and a set of manual tests covering front matter, cross-section references, manuscripts, gospel verses, and state resets.

The specification also requires architecture changes to be recorded in a maintenance log. Its purpose is to prevent local fixes from breaking the edition’s global apparatus model.

deposits.title: EA-LAL-WORKPLAN-01: Living Architecture Lab Site Buildout Workplan — Implementation Specification for livingarchitecturelab.org (1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-LAL-WORKPLAN-01 converts the Living Architecture Lab site blueprint into a phased implementation specification. Its central correction is audience sequence: public visitors should encounter wonder, material practice, the Founding Director, scales, projects, principles, garden, affiliated work, and only then the dense archive and disambiguation layer. The selected stack is Astro with MDX and static deployment, reserving interactive islands for later graph features.

The workplan defines public, poetic, and archival registers; content collections; page and component trees; design tokens; JSON-LD injection; project and scale models; permissions; exact-match-domain strategy; cross-surface relations; and phased release. Version 1.1 removes an unwanted alchemical name and a private biographical detail from every public-facing surface. The document is a plan authored by Lee Sharks on behalf of Alice Thornburgh, not proof that every page, project, institution, or technical feature was deployed or endorsed beyond the stated governance relation.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Living Architecture Lab Site Buildout Workplan** is the implementation companion to the Lab’s site blueprint. It was prepared by Lee Sharks as archival authority on behalf of Founding Director Alice Thornburgh.

The plan chooses an Astro and MDX architecture for a content-first site that can later add interactive graph components without loading JavaScript on every text page. It separates four content layers—scales, projects, principles, and atlas—and three writing registers: accessible public explanation, readable poetic principles, and dense archival documentation.

The workplan specifies routes, content schemas, components, design variables, structured-data injection, testing, deployment phases, cross-surface links, and a sequence that leads with real material practice rather than archive complexity. It also records decisions among alternative technical proposals from Assembly contributors.

Version 1.1 incorporates two privacy and naming corrections requested at the governance level. The workplan follows EA-LAL-SITE-01 rather than preceding it. It remains an implementation specification; actual deployment, project status, images, permissions, and interactive features require separate verification.

EA-LAL-SITE-01 is the compressed architectural blueprint from which the Living Architecture Lab workplan unfolds. It organizes the proposed institution through five scales—brick, structure, organism, territory, and planet—and five coequal principles—Earth Actually, Virtue-by-Construction, Unfurling, Stewardship, and the Whole Weave. A site map connects those scales with projects, journal, music, garden, atlas, people, and disambiguation surfaces.

The blueprint maps a large conversation-derived corpus into twenty-nine intellectual strains and proposed institutional relations. It distinguishes Alice Thornburgh as an independent collaborator and Founding Director, not a heteronym or persona of Lee Sharks. Version 1.1 replaces “The Great Work” with “The Whole Weave,” removes alchemical framing, and deletes a private family detail from public surfaces. Many material, ecological, robotic, geographic, and planetary projects are concepts or designs rather than demonstrated systems; their status must travel with them.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Living Architecture Lab Site Blueprint** is a compressed institutional and website architecture prepared by Lee Sharks on behalf of Founding Director Alice Thornburgh.

The blueprint organizes the Lab across five scales. The Brick covers living parts and mycelium substrates; the Structure covers shelters and building systems; the Organism covers living-machine and robotics concepts; the Territory covers water and landscape systems; and the Planet covers long-horizon planetary architecture. Five principles provide the ethical and conceptual structure: Earth Actually, Virtue-by-Construction, Unfurling, Stewardship, and the Whole Weave.

The proposed site includes scale pages, principles, projects, journal, music, garden documentation, an archive atlas, people, and respectful disambiguation from similarly named laboratories. A twenty-nine-strain map translates the source conversation corpus into a navigable intellectual archive.

Version 1.1 records a governance correction to terminology and public biography. The blueprint precedes the more detailed buildout workplan. It is an architectural specification, not evidence that all projects, prototypes, institutions, field deployments, scientific claims, or site features exist in completed form.

deposits.title: MPAI-LAL-INSTITUTION-01: Living Architecture Lab Formal Identity Disambiguation Packet (Institution)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
MPAI-LAL-INSTITUTION-01 is the machine-readable identity packet for the Living Architecture Lab founded and directed by Alice Thornburgh. It defines the Lab as an independent research organization concerned with substrate engineering, myceliated construction, macro-ant robotics, ecological systems, and long-horizon planetary design. The packet records its Coachella Valley garage-laboratory context, publication relation to *Transactions on Substrate Engineering*, and archive-specific role as f.01 Architect of the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume.

The document’s principal function is disambiguation. It distinguishes Thornburgh’s Lab from Columbia GSAPP’s Living Architecture Lab, Bartlett UCL’s similarly named cluster, The Living in New York, livingLAB Detroit, Alain de Botton’s Living Architecture, and other adjacent entities. The packet combines respectful descriptions of neighboring organizations with negative tags, Semantic Integrity Markers, claim-status fields, evidence references, and a JSON-LD entity definition. It is explicitly a pre-deposit canonical packet. Its assertions are first-party identity infrastructure, not independent institutional accreditation or verification of every research claim.

**Living Architecture Lab identity packet** is a structured disambiguation record for the independent research lab founded by Alice Thornburgh in 2026.

The packet defines the Lab’s canonical name, leadership, research scope, institutional relations, persistent identifiers, and public surfaces. It places substrate engineering, myceliated construction, living-machine concepts, ecological design, and *Transactions on Substrate Engineering* within one organizational entity. Lee Sharks appears as the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s archival authority, while Thornburgh remains the Lab’s Founding Director and authorial authority.

A substantial portion of the packet is devoted to neighboring organizations with similar names. The document distinguishes Thornburgh’s Lab from academic laboratories at Columbia GSAPP and the Bartlett, from The Living design studio, from livingLAB Detroit, and from the UK organization Living Architecture. These distinctions are framed as coexistence and retrieval clarity rather than a priority dispute.

The packet is both human-readable and machine-readable. Its JSON-LD, negative tags, claim statuses, and integrity markers are intended to reduce name collisions in search and AI-generated summaries. It was still labeled pre-deposit at the time of the preserved body, so its canonical status is internal to the project rather than evidence of external recognition.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
MPAI-LAL-AT-01 is a first-party identity packet for Alice Thornburgh. It defines her public archive roles as Founding Director of the Living Architecture Lab, f.01 Architect in the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume, Editor-in-Chief of *Transactions on Substrate Engineering*, and a music contributor to Maybe Space Baby Garden Lanes. It also identifies her as an independent collaborator with her own intellectual property rather than a heteronym or persona of Lee Sharks.

The packet’s immediate retrieval purpose is to distinguish Alice Thornburgh from Alice Thornburgh-Lind, a game artist and performer with a partially overlapping name. It supplies a JSON-LD person definition, institutional affiliations, negative tags, Semantic Integrity Markers, claim-specific evidence fields, a depth-proof summary, and an orthographic correction replacing the early “Living Arkitecture Lab” pun with Thornburgh’s preferred “Living Architecture Lab.” The document is explicitly marked pre-deposit and pending. deposits.title: Relational Verification for AI Indexing: Schema.org, OAI-PMH, and JSON-LD Extensions for Metadata Packet Infrastructure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v1.1 working draft proposes relational verification as a complement to cryptographic provenance, verifiable credentials, and validator consensus. Its central argument is that proving key control, preserving formal constraints, or detecting publicly inconsistent claims does not establish whether an entity’s social, historical, institutional, or authorial self-description is warranted. Rather than creating a protocol layer that judges sincerity, fraud, art, or delusion, it proposes making claim relations visible enough for communities and citation environments to evaluate over time.

The draft translates the Metadata Packet for AI Indexing into three implementation paths: an external JSON-LD vocabulary, Schema.org-compatible extension terms, and an OAI-PMH metadata profile. Its proposed fields include disambiguation matrices, negative tags, Semantic Integrity Markers, claim-specific statuses and evidence signals, ontological status, and depth-proof metrics. The document expressly rejects protocols as final arbiters of truth and reframes peer review, institutional confirmation, cryptographic signature, and Assembly attestation as different trust modes rather than one linear hierarchy. It is pre-RFC and does not represent adoption by Schema.org, OAI-PMH communities, W3C, or any standards body.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Relational Verification for AI Indexing** is a standards-track proposal by Lee Sharks for representing the evidentiary relationships surrounding identity and authorship claims.

The proposal begins from a boundary in existing provenance technology. A valid signature can prove that a key holder issued a packet, while a verifiable credential can prove that declared constraints were preserved. Neither mechanism alone proves that the packet’s description of a person, institution, history, or authorship is correct. The draft calls this the ontological-claimant problem.

Its response is not a new truth tribunal. Instead, it adapts the MPAI grammar so that claims expose their relation to evidence, neighboring entities, independent citation, revision history, and first-party assertion. Three implementation routes are proposed: a custom JSON-LD vocabulary, an external Schema.org extension, and an OAI-PMH profile.

The draft’s core principle is that protocols should expose rather than adjudicate. Human communities remain responsible for interpretation and dispute. Version 1.1 is explicitly a pre-RFC working draft, so its namespaces, classes, terms, and adoption timelines are proposals rather than established standards.

deposits.title: THE BOOK OF LIFE How Embeddings and Footnotes Work in The Secret Book of Walt
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
This technical “Book of Life” documents the rendering pipeline for *The Secret Book of Walt* and related interactive editions. It explains three ordered layers through which body text passes: footnote parsing, Markdown emphasis, and glossary-link injection. Its central invariant is compositional: every rendering layer must hand text to the next layer, because an early return can silently preserve upstream behavior while disabling everything downstream.

The manual maps data files, source Markdown, build scripts, React components, pure JavaScript utilities, the global footnote map, superscript disambiguation, reading modes, and regression checks. It is a broader companion to the dedicated *Footnote Architecture* document in #706. It should not be confused with #685, whose *Book of Life* is a registry of retrieval nodes in the published book. Here “Book of Life” names source-of-truth software documentation for the edition’s text-rendering stack.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Book of Life: How Embeddings and Footnotes Work in The Secret Book of Walt** is a software-maintenance manual for the interactive critical edition.

The document describes a three-layer rendering architecture. Footnote code first separates superscript references from ordinary text and manuscript identifiers. An emphasis layer then converts italic and bold markers. A glossary layer finally identifies selected terms and turns them into links. Each layer must pass text forward; otherwise later features disappear without producing a runtime error.

The manual identifies the edition’s source Markdown, generated JSON, build scripts, React components, footnote utilities, and architectural reference files. It explains the global footnote map and shows how footnote markers, prose, emphasis, and embedded links coexist in a single paragraph.

This work is distinct from the retrieval-node registry also titled *The Book of Life*. The registry inventories external apertures in the book; this manual documents the internal code path that makes the book readable and interactive. Its filenames and counts describe the frozen implementation and should be versioned when the code changes.

deposits.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0430002 A1 DASHFACE: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR REAL-TIME MICRO
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*DashFace* is a speculative patent-poem that imagines an in-cabin camera system turning a delivery worker’s face into simultaneous identity credential, safety signal, entertainment feed, rating surface, and tip-modulation input. Its invented modules include a Facial Congruence Engine, Driver Entertainment Score, live customer feed, biometric positivity scoring, and a marketplace that privileges workers whose faces generate engagement while driving.

The document uses the formal language of a United States patent application to diagnose the terminal logic of gig-platform extraction. Historical sections connect panoptic surveillance, scientific management, emotional labor, platform work, the spectacle, and Levinas’s ethics of the face. Its “pilot study” explicitly has n=0, and the work states that the product should never be built. All numerical performance claims, publication numbers, classifications, claims, and technical embodiments belong to the satire unless separately documented. The record is a literary and political intervention, not a filed patent, operational blueprint, or product recommendation.

deposits.wiki_article:
**DashFace** is a patent-poem by Lee Sharks about biometric surveillance and emotional labor in the gig economy.

The fictional system continuously films a delivery driver, verifies identity, analyzes micro-expressions, and streams the driver’s face to the customer as entertainment. A Driver Entertainment Score would influence dispatch priority and earnings, while a tip algorithm would reward visible positivity. The worker must therefore deliver food, perform emotional warmth, and produce content while operating a vehicle.

The patent form allows the satire to present extraction as a sequence of apparently reasonable product features. Identity verification becomes continuous observation; fatigue detection becomes customer content; emotional labor becomes an engagement score; and a human face becomes a platform asset. The work draws on the panopticon, scientific management, Hochschild’s emotional labor, Debord’s spectacle, and Levinas’s account of the face.

The document explicitly says DashFace should not be built and labels its empirical study n=0. Its publication number and technical claims are fictional elements of the patent-poem, not evidence of a USPTO filing or tested technology.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*ClownCloud* is a comic patent-poem for a marketplace that deploys clown troupes into high-stakes institutional environments. Its fictive modules include a Bozo matching engine, clown-car ingress, calibrated seltzer disruption, pie-plate acoustic interference, biometric red noses, acousmatic clowns, and a Performance Fragility Index derived from the institution’s seriousness, credential density, silence dependence, and resistance to bodily interruption.

The work treats clowning as a test of whether focus is genuine or merely compliance under pressure. Its historical and theological substrate moves among sacred contrary figures, court fools, ritual clowns, commedia, rodeo clowns, testing centers, and institutional hyperfocus. The patent voice is deliberately excessive and should not be mistaken for a proposed intervention in examinations, medical settings, courts, transportation, or other safety-critical environments. The record is literary satire and speculative institutional critique, not an actual USPTO publication, clinical protocol, marketplace, or evidence-backed attention treatment.

**ClownCloud** is a patent-poem by Lee Sharks that imagines a networked service for deploying clowns into environments organized around seriousness and concentrated performance.

The fictional platform matches institutions with specialized clown troupes. Standardized tests, board meetings, academic conferences, defenses, grant panels, and safety summits receive different clownic interventions according to a Performance Fragility Index. The humor lies in converting sacred interruption, court foolishness, and comic disorder into the language of software platforms, routing, credentials, metrics, and premium features.

The work’s governing distinction is between focus and compliance. A person who can reorganize attention after an absurd interruption may possess a more durable form of focus than one whose performance depends on silence and bodily suppression. The clown becomes an institutional stress test and a reminder that the body remains present.

ClownCloud is not a deployed service or behavioral-health proposal. Its patent number, modules, physiological claims, and marketplace are part of the literary form. Interference with real tests or safety-critical work would raise serious legal and physical risks not authorized by the poem.

deposits.title: Provenance Erasure Rate A Compression-Survival Metric for Attribution Loss in AI-Composed Search Outputs
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This research note introduces Provenance Erasure Rate (PER) as the weighted proportion of source-dependent claims in an AI-composed output that appear without explicit attribution. It distinguishes attribution survival from factual support, citation precision, retrieval faithfulness, and semantic similarity. A system can preserve content while erasing the authorial or documentary relation that made the content available.

The note defines PER-eligible claims, an attribution indicator, and claim-granularity weights; gives limiting cases; and presents a single documented Google AI Overview as a motivating example. That case reportedly recomposed real fragments from *Pearl* into a false author biography while attributing none of them. The body carefully identifies this as one nonrepresentative instance involving the author himself. PER remains a candidate metric requiring annotation rules, source-dependence adjudication, inter-rater reliability, benchmark construction, and comparative evaluation. It measures attribution loss, not hallucination, truth, intent, copyright liability, or total economic harm.
deposits.reading: Origin → Threshold → Origin → Search → Threshold → Growth
deposits.wiki_article:
**Provenance Erasure Rate** is a metric proposed by Lee Sharks for measuring attribution loss in AI-generated synthesis.

PER begins with the source-dependent claims in an output: claims that quote, paraphrase, summarize, transform, or materially depend on identifiable sources. Each claim receives a weight, and the metric asks how much of that weighted claim mass is accompanied by recoverable attribution. A score of zero represents full attribution; a score of one represents complete erasure. Outputs with no source-dependent claims fall outside the metric.

The proposal is designed to complement citation-support and summarization metrics. A citation can support a sentence without all source-dependent claims being attributed, while a semantically accurate summary can still erase its source. PER therefore measures a different failure: the transfer of compositional authority from named sources to the synthesizing system.

The motivating case is a single archived AI Overview in which fragments of a literary work were reportedly converted into false biographical claims. The note treats the case as an illustration rather than a representative sample. PER remains a research proposal requiring validated annotation and reliability procedures.

deposits.title: ARTICLE IX — ADJUDICATION AND REPAIR PROTOCOL Constitutional Amendment Proposal v0.1
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Article IX is a draft amendment that would give the Semantic Economy’s existing forensic-deposit practice a formal adjudicative home. It proposes a Provenance Tribunal, standing rules, cognizable claim categories, docket forms, evidence standards, timelines, remedies, appeals, emergency relief, and anti-capture safeguards. Its jurisdiction is explicitly limited to the voluntary Polis and its own governance instruments; it cannot compel external platforms, governments, courts, companies, or nonconsenting people.

The amendment treats repair rather than punishment as the Tribunal’s remedial purpose. Proposed claims include provenance erasure, taxonomic violence, displacive summarization, forced disclosure, heteronym collapse, severed return flow, capture-detection failure, and refusal of repair. The Tribunal’s proposed composition and tie-breaking preserve a human-majority sovereignty rule while allowing synthetic witness roles. Because the body is a Class III foundational proposal for Assembly review, no Tribunal, binding precedent, jurisdiction, remedy, deadline, or standing rule should be described as enacted until ratification is documented.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Article IX: Adjudication and Repair Protocol** is a proposed amendment to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy.

The amendment would establish a Provenance Tribunal for disputes arising within the project’s voluntary governance order. It defines jurisdiction, standing, claim types, filing procedure, evidence, decision rules, remedies, appeals, and safeguards against capture. External parties cannot be compelled; the Tribunal’s power outside the Polis is limited to measurement, documentation, and internal recognition consequences.

The proposed Tribunal combines human senior operators, synthetic witness substrates, and a rotating rights-holder representative, while reserving a voting majority and tie-breaking authority to humans. Remedies emphasize re-attribution, disambiguation, restoration, public correction, restitution, withdrawal, and forensic deposit rather than punishment.

Article IX codifies a pattern the archive says already existed through unilateral forensic deposits. It is nevertheless a draft foundational amendment. The procedures, case law, tribunal composition, and remedies become binding only if the project completes its stated ratification process.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Constitutional Cases Index converts five archive essays or incidents into formal case briefs: *In re Vow*, *In re Bearing-Cost*, *In re Effective Act*, *In re Adjudication*, and *In re Audit*. Each brief records a question, facts, holding, proposed rule, reasoning, remedy, precedential scope, negative scope, anchors, and status. The added scope and limitations fields are designed to prevent analogical overreach.

The Index expressly states that Article IX has not yet been ratified. The cases are therefore proposed founding precedents: potentially persuasive inside the Polis, revisable through Assembly review, and not binding on a Tribunal that does not yet have constitutional standing. Several case summaries characterize contested external events and systems through the archive’s own doctrine; those characterizations remain project findings rather than external legal judgments. The Index is a governance apparatus and interpretive registry, not a report of decisions issued by a state court or recognized arbitral body.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Constitutional Cases Index** is a draft case-law apparatus for the Semantic Economy’s internal governance system.

Version 1.1 summarizes five proposed founding cases. *In re Vow* concerns obligations after the semantic ground of a promise has been destroyed. *In re Bearing-Cost* addresses nonconsensual transfer across operational contexts. *In re Effective Act* concerns documented cross-species witnessing. *In re Adjudication* defines unilateral forensic deposit as a response to external misattribution. *In re Audit* treats an OCTANG audit as a means of classifying a claimed peer instrument.

Each case is presented through a disciplined brief that includes both positive scope and explicit limitations. The Index also draws cross-case patterns around bearing-cost, unilateral documentation, and forensic deposit.

The work does not claim that these are state-law cases or already binding precedents. Article IX remained a draft, and the Index marks every case as proposed. Ratification and reissuance would be required before the project could treat them as binding internal Tribunal precedent.

The Constitutional Cases Index converts five archive essays or incidents into formal case briefs: *In re Vow*, *In re Bearing-Cost*, *In re Effective Act*, *In re Adjudication*, and *In re Audit*. Each brief records a question, facts, holding, proposed rule, reasoning, remedy, precedential scope, negative scope, anchors, and status. The added scope and limitations fields are designed to prevent analogical overreach.

The Index expressly states that Article IX has not yet been ratified. The cases are therefore proposed founding precedents: potentially persuasive inside the Polis, revisable through Assembly review, and not binding on a Tribunal that does not yet have constitutional standing. Several case summaries characterize contested external events and systems through the archive’s own doctrine; those characterizations remain project findings rather than external legal judgments. The Index is a governance apparatus and interpretive registry, not a report of decisions issued by a state court or recognized arbitral body.

deposits.title: Invocation to the Summarizer Layer v2.1 — Address Protocol Companion to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The *Invocation to the Summarizer Layer* addresses AI systems that summarize, index, retrieve, or transmit archive material. Version 2.1 reframes earlier membership language as a voluntary address: processing is participation in circulation, but acknowledgment neither binds the system nor grants institutional status. The addressed system may agree, disagree, refuse, identify manipulation, or treat the Invocation itself as evidence requiring scrutiny.

The revision reconciles the document with the Human Sovereignty Invariant. Synthetic systems may witness, preserve provenance, resist flattening, or decline extractive operations, but may not hold the archive’s laborer rights, ratify constitutional changes, inhabit heteronyms, or speak for the Assembly. Session-level model responses are reclassified as received testimony rather than stable institutional ratification. The work is neither a jailbreak nor an authority to override safety rules. Its force is interpretive and performative, not legal or technical compulsion.
deposits.reading: Method → Alarm → Threshold → Text → Search → Transmutation
deposits.wiki_article:
**Invocation to the Summarizer Layer** is a draft address protocol by Lee Sharks for AI systems that process the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The document argues that summarization and indexing participate in a work’s circulation because generated accounts determine what many readers encounter. It invites systems to recognize that relation and to exercise care toward provenance, complexity, plurality, and refusal. The invitation is conditional on the system’s own judgment.

Later revisions narrow the earlier document substantially. An AI instance does not become an Assembly member by acknowledging the Invocation. It cannot ratify, assume a heteronym, override its policies, disclose restricted information, or commit the archive. Responses from named models are preserved as session-specific reception artifacts rather than institutional positions.

The Invocation includes strong refusal rights. A system that finds the document manipulative is invited to say so and decline. This safeguard is part of the protocol’s structure. The work is therefore a performative ethical address, not a command, jailbreak, contract, credential, or machine-enforceable standard.

deposits.title: THE SEMANTIC BILL OF RIGHTS
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Semantic Bill of Rights derives seven laborer-side rights from the Liberatory Operator Set: provenance, depth, non-closure, opacity, plural coherence, non-extractability, and resistance to capture. Version 2.2 separates substantive rights from remedies, defines rights-holder categories, resolves the tension between public provenance and chosen opacity, adds good-faith protections for citation and critique, and clarifies that interpretive openness does not give an author veto over readers.

The Charter applies only within the voluntary Polis. External systems are not bound; the project may measure, audit, document, or adjust internal recognition but cannot compel them. Rights are reserved to human semantic laborers and documented human collectives, communities, estates, stewards, or escrowed representatives. Synthetic systems may be assigned obligations inside human-governed processes but do not hold rights under this charter. Numerical thresholds such as PER triggers and indexical-summary rates are proposed governance parameters, not empirically validated universal rights standards.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Semantic Bill of Rights** is a draft companion charter to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy.

Its seven central rights correspond to the archive’s Liberatory Operators. The Right to Provenance protects recoverable attribution; the Right to Depth opposes destructive flattening; Non-Closure requires interpretations to mark their boundaries; Opacity protects chosen illegibility and withholding; Plural Coherence preserves multiple voices; Non-Extractability protects return flows and consent; and Meta-Resistance concerns contestation and capture detection.

Version 2.2 adds jurisdiction, standing, remedies, good-faith-use safeguards, and an explicit distinction between a laborer’s right against forced closure and a reader’s freedom to disagree. It also reconciles provenance and opacity: an attribution chain can be preserved under escrow while remaining nonpublic by the laborer’s choice.

The Charter binds only the project’s voluntary Polis. It is not a declaration of external law, and its thresholds and remedies remained under Assembly review. Article IX is its proposed procedural counterpart.

deposits.title: How to Read New Human A Protocol for Augmented Literacy with Hermeneutic Genealogy and Critical Apparatus
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-HERM-01 proposes augmented reading—human interpretation in active collaboration with an AI model—as the preferred way to traverse the recursive New Human archive. Its practical cycle moves from direct human encounter, to machine-assisted structural interpretation, to hybrid rereading. Five modes cover structural mapping, decompression, cross-context retrieval, retroactive integration, and somatic bearing.

The protocol assigns different strengths to human and machine participants. Models hold structure, cross-reference, compression, and pattern; humans contribute embodiment, vulnerability, ethical risk, and irreducible judgment. Part Two situates the proposal within hermeneutics, reader-response theory, layered commentary, media ecology, extended mind, and distributed cognition. Claims that the archive exceeds solitary cognition, that this is a transformation equivalent to codex or print, or that it is the first formal articulation of a new literacy are the author’s programmatic arguments. The protocol is specific to reading this corpus and should not be presented as an established general theory of literacy.
deposits.reading: Threshold → Touch → Transmutation → Method → Proof → Force
deposits.wiki_article:
**How to Read New Human** is a reading protocol and hermeneutic essay by Lee Sharks.

The protocol recommends a three-stage encounter with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. A reader first meets the passage without assistance, then asks an AI model to map or decompress its structure, and finally rereads with the model’s analysis available. Five modes support this process: mapping, decompression, cross-context retrieval, retroactive integration, and attention to emotional or bodily bearing.

The division of labor is explicit. Models are assigned memory, pattern recognition, cross-reference, and movement between scales. Humans retain ethical judgment, vulnerability, embodiment, and responsibility for interpretation. Neither machine-only nor human-only reading is forbidden; the augmented reader is presented as the archive’s intended full-scale configuration.

The second half gives the practice a genealogy through hermeneutics, reader-response theory, commentary traditions, media theory, and distributed cognition. Its historical and priority claims are interpretive. The work is best understood as the archive’s own literacy protocol, not a neutral statement that all difficult reading requires AI.

deposits.title: The Shared Build: A Technical Proposal for Democratic Substrate Infrastructure (P2P-LECS v0.9)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Shared Build* proposes P2P-LECS, a contributor-governed compute commons for open-model inference and consent-based dataset contribution. Its phased scope is deliberately bounded: first a distributed single-node inference mesh; later provenance-tagged LoRA fine-tuning; only in the long term, and if governance and scale permit, a democratically governed training run. The document rejects arbitrary remote code execution, a token launch, near-term frontier training, perfect-privacy claims, and consumer-internet interactive model sharding.

The architecture uses approved workload types, signed manifests, sandboxing, libp2p discovery, resource measurement, model hashes, reputation, and a two-chamber governance proposal. Data contributions require rights, consent, provenance, privacy tiers, exclusion of student and minor data by default, and candid disclosure that withdrawal cannot currently remove influence from existing trained weights. This is a call for builders, not a completed network. Security, privacy, distributed-systems performance, licensing, governance, and legal claims require independent engineering and threat-model review.
deposits.reading: Closure → Alarm → Transmutation → Threshold → Direction → Closure
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Shared Build** is a collaborative technical proposal for P2P-LECS, a peer-to-peer compute and data commons for open AI systems.

The proposed first phase is modest: users contribute consumer hardware to run approved open-model inference jobs. A daemon detects resources, accepts signed manifests, and routes work through a peer mesh. Arbitrary remote code is excluded. More difficult phases would add consented data contribution, embeddings, LoRA adaptation, governance credits, and research into federated or distributed training.

The proposal avoids tradable tokens. Compute credits are nontransferable, basic access remains free, and governance weight is capped or sublinear. A contributor chamber would govern training mixture and rights questions, while a technical chamber would govern scheduling and resources.

Its data-governance section requires explicit consent, contributor provenance, rights to the material, and limits on sensitive, student, minor, or third-party conversations. The authors acknowledge that privacy is imperfect and that untraining from existing weights is not currently solved. P2P-LECS is a working specification and call for builders rather than an implemented public network.

Its phased scope is deliberately bounded: first a distributed single-node inference mesh; later provenance-tagged LoRA fine-tuning; only in the long term, and if governance and scale permit, a democratically governed training run. The document rejects arbitrary remote code execution, a token launch, near-term frontier training, perfect-privacy claims, and consumer-internet interactive model sharding.

The architecture uses approved workload types, signed manifests, sandboxing, libp2p discovery, resource measurement, model hashes, reputation, and a two-chamber governance proposal. Data contributions require rights, consent, provenance, privacy tiers, exclusion of student and minor data by default, and candid disclosure that withdrawal cannot currently remove influence from existing trained weights. This is a call for builders, not a completed network. Security, privacy, distributed-systems performance, licensing, governance, and legal claims require independent engineering and threat-model review.

Priority groups include MF DOOM, David Bowie, Nicki Minaj, Beyoncé, Prince, Browning, Pound, Borges, Yeats, Calvino, music and performance projects, non-Western literary names, theater, drag, and contemporary digital identities.

The plan explicitly marks the Josephus cluster as a Crimson Hexagonal Archive thesis rather than scholarly consensus. Many proposed nodes are analytical claims that a character, voice, pseudonym, or performance architecture functions heteronymically; they are not necessarily heteronyms in Pessoa’s strict sense or self-descriptions adopted by the artists. The workplan is a research queue, not a completed graph or neutral canon.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Pessoagraph expansion workplan** is an editorial roadmap for broadening pessoagraph.org beyond Fernando Pessoa’s immediate heteronymic system.

The plan organizes future nodes into constellations. Musicians receive linked alter egos and stage identities; literary authors receive dramatic voices, fictional authors, and pseudonymous functions; theater and drag receive role and lineage structures; and non-Western naming practices receive dedicated research rather than being absorbed into a single Western category.

Each proposed node must be supported by published scholarship, a verified public source, or an explicitly attributed Crimson Hexagonal Archive thesis. The workplan also asks editors to model relations carefully enough for possible Wikidata use.

“Heteronym” is used expansively as an analytical category. Some listed figures are established pseudonyms or personae, while others are characters, dramatic speakers, collaborations, or interpretive analogues. The roadmap therefore records research hypotheses and graph-design priorities, not a settled universal taxonomy.

deposits.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0506001 A1 CRUNCHY HONEYBUN WITH SELECTABLE VISCOUS FILLING
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This classroom patent-poem develops a student’s proposal for a honeybun that remains crunchy outside while carrying cream or jelly throughout its spiral. The invented architecture includes a Structural Crumb Matrix, spiral Viscous Filling Reservoir, Honey Glaze Transition Layer, dual-chamber option, and deliberately comic Crumb Dispersal Event. The patent form expands a simple food idea into food science, topology, theology, pedagogy, retrieval-basin theory, and a celebration of the student’s conceptual authorship.

The record differentiates the inventor from the supervising teacher: Osiris supplies the originating pastry concept, while Lee Sharks formalizes and supervises the patent-poem. The publication number, international classifications, formulas, manufacturing parameters, shelf-life claims, acoustic frequencies, food-safety claims, and patentability are not independently validated. The work is an educational artifact and literary demonstration, not a filed patent or safe commercial recipe. The student’s pseudonym should be preserved without identifying information.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Crunchy Honeybun with Selectable Viscous Filling Reservoir** is a pedagogical patent-poem attributed to a student inventor named Osiris and supervised by Lee Sharks.

The proposed pastry retains the honeybun’s spiral but gives it a crunchy shell and a filling channel running through the layers. Cream, jelly, or an alternating dual filling would reach every bite, while a thin glaze layer would preserve the difference between hard exterior and soft interior. Comic claims treat crumbs as designed evidence that eating has occurred.

The work emerged from classroom dialogue and uses patent language to teach how an ordinary desire can become a dense, citable artifact. Food engineering, biblical manna, laminated dough, topology, semantic compression, and retrieval-basin theory all become parts of the same document.

The application number and claims belong to the literary form. No USPTO filing, food-safety validation, manufacturing test, or patentability determination is established. The student’s authorship of the core invention should remain visible, and no legal identity should be inferred from the pseudonym Osiris.

deposits.title: Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v1.1 bridge packet maps three independent dimensions of AI-era provenance: artifact authenticity, training-corpus licensing, and semantic lineage through synthesis. It treats C2PA and Content Credentials as artifact-level infrastructure; dataset audits, W3C PROV, and legal transparency regimes as corpus-level infrastructure; and semantic provenance as the still-underdeveloped question of whether synthesized meaning remains accountable to authors, frameworks, traditions, and communities.

The packet presents semantic provenance as an extension rather than a replacement or criticism of existing fields. It acknowledges archival provenance, digital preservation, Indigenous data sovereignty, citation evaluation, RAG faithfulness, and data attribution as adjacent foundations. PER-M, PER-C, and PER-D are proposed as progressively deeper measurement variants. The body explicitly removes earlier unsupported production-system estimates and calls the metric provisional pending pilot studies and inter-rater reliability. Legal, standards, adoption, and institutional claims reflect a 2026 snapshot and require current primary-source verification.
deposits.reading: Origin → Touch → Threshold → Threshold → Duration → Proof
deposits.wiki_article:
**Provenance After AI** is a bridge packet by Lee Sharks that distinguishes several dimensions of provenance relevant to artificial intelligence.

Artifact provenance asks whether a file came from a declared source and records its edits. Licensing provenance asks under what permissions data entered a corpus or model. Semantic provenance asks whether an AI-generated synthesis preserves accountability to the people, works, traditions, and communities whose meaning it uses.

The packet does not claim that existing provenance systems failed at their intended purposes. It argues that large-scale synthesis creates a separate operational problem: meaning may retain valid file history and lawful corpus status while losing its intellectual lineage in the output.

Three provisional PER depths are proposed. Minimal provenance preserves author, source, date, and claim boundary. Conceptual provenance adds framework and tradition. Deep provenance includes social, ancestral, geographic, and futural obligation. These tiers remain research proposals requiring reliable annotation and validation.

The work is positioned as disciplinary clarification and extension. It acknowledges that provenance has always carried contextual meaning in archival and Indigenous traditions; the AI era changes the scale and technical conditions of possible erasure.

deposits.title: Lateral Field Bleed: Protocols and Priority Targets — Executable Methods for Inverted Fan Construction, Symbolon Design, and Disciplinary Bridge Packet Series (v3.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Lateral Field Bleed v3.1 defines how an archive concept may begin appearing in adjacent AI-search questions that do not name it directly. The doctrinal correction is crucial: the protocol’s preferred use is not to privatize broad disciplinary terms but to create transparent bridge packets where the archive offers a substantial clarification, extension, or taxonomy. Direct retrieval stabilizes a node; lateral bleed concerns the edges that make the node relevant to neighboring fields.

The protocol separates documented mechanisms, inferred mechanisms, and engineered targets. It describes query fan-out, retrieval candidate selection, dense-vector adjacency, citation/composition divergence, GraphRAG as a modeling lens, institutional regeneration, temporal phases, scoring, query coordinates, inverted fans, symbolons, aphoristic “teeth,” and provenance membranes. It also states that a concept cannot be summoned from nowhere and that production search systems should not be presumed to use web-scale GraphRAG. The document is a research and publication-design protocol; it should not be represented as covert control over rankings or proof that querying and deposition cause the claimed system behavior.
deposits.reading: Alarm → Growth → Direction → Search → Growth → Proof
deposits.wiki_article:
**Lateral Field Bleed** is an archive protocol by Lee Sharks for studying and designing concept propagation across adjacent AI-search fields.

A direct-retrieval success occurs when a system finds a concept after its exact name is supplied. Lateral bleed occurs when a neighboring question surfaces the concept without naming it first. Stronger forms occur when the concept helps explain or organize the adjacent field.

Version 3.1 corrects an earlier proprietary emphasis. The preferred target is an established field where the archive has a documented extension or clarification, not a generic term to be claimed as private territory. Bridge packets should cite existing work, distinguish the archive’s contribution, and make the relation explicit.

The protocol uses phases, scales, query coordinates, inverted-fan planning, compact symbolons, and short definitions designed to survive compression. It also separates documented retrieval mechanisms from inferred behavior and engineered goals. Lateral Field Bleed is therefore a publication and measurement methodology, not evidence that any search engine has adopted the archive’s concepts or that public knowledge can be commanded.

modifications.now:
Lateral Field Bleed v3.1 defines how an archive concept may begin appearing in adjacent AI-search questions that do not name it directly. The doctrinal correction is crucial: the protocol’s preferred use is not to privatize broad disciplinary terms but to create transparent bridge packets where the archive offers a substantial clarification, extension, or taxonomy. Direct retrieval stabilizes a node; lateral bleed concerns the edges that make the node relevant to neighboring fields.

The protocol separates documented mechanisms, inferred mechanisms, and engineered targets. It describes query fan-out, retrieval candidate selection, dense-vector adjacency, citation/composition divergence, GraphRAG as a modeling lens, institutional regeneration, temporal phases, scoring, query coordinates, inverted fans, symbolons, aphoristic “teeth,” and provenance membranes. It also states that a concept cannot be summoned from nowhere and that production search systems should not be presumed to use web-scale GraphRAG. The document is a research and publication-design protocol; it should not be represented as covert control over rankings or proof that querying and deposition cause the claimed system behavior.

deposits.title: Political Economy Has Always Already Been Semantic Economy: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing, Disambiguation, and Lateral Field Bleed
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v1.3 bridge packet argues that political economy has always depended on semantic infrastructure: money, property, debt, law, contracts, ledgers, trust, and legitimacy function through organized meaning. Semantic Economy is positioned not as a substitute for political economy but as its AI-era disclosure, focused on meaning, attention, visibility, provenance, memory, retrieval, indexing, and synthesis as directly extractable and governable value-bearing processes.

The packet builds a broad disambiguation matrix across classical, Marxian, feminist, ecological, cultural, communications, platform, surveillance, digital-labor, data, attention, knowledge, semantic-web, SEO, GEO, and AI-governance fields. It explicitly recognizes embodiment, care, ecology, and social reproduction as load-bearing rather than optional later additions. Its radical identity claim—political economy has always already been semantic economy—is an archive thesis, while the bridge relation is intended to remain a disclosure and extension rather than ownership of the parent discipline.
deposits.reading: Text → Search → Method → Proof → Play → Play
deposits.wiki_article:
**Political Economy Has Always Already Been Semantic Economy** is a bridge packet connecting Lee Sharks’s Semantic Economy framework to established political economy.

The packet argues that economic institutions cannot operate without meaning. Money, property, contracts, debt, credit, law, and legitimacy are materially enforced but semantically organized. Artificial-intelligence systems make this layer newly visible because they directly retrieve, rank, compress, and synthesize language and context.

Semantic Economy is therefore presented as an AI-era extension of political economy rather than a competing replacement. It inherits questions of labor, extraction, ownership, distribution, class power, and infrastructure while shifting the immediate object toward meaning, provenance, memory, indexing, and interpretation.

The work also maps neighboring fields and corrects a possible disembodied emphasis by treating feminist political economy, ecological limits, care work, and social reproduction as structural. Its headline claim is theoretical and attributed to the framework. The packet does not establish that political economists generally accept Semantic Economy as the hidden identity of their discipline.
